decisions.title: Nudge payout sweeps full balance to caller-supplied recipient
decisions.reason: Genuine MEV/mempool-race vulnerability in BatchNFTMinter. Not addressed by any documented intentional design in phoenix-nft-staking/CLAUDE.md (which covers NFTStaker semantics). Owner centralization is acknowledged but this is a public mempool race that affects honest owners equally — not a centralization issue. Severity hint: high.

decisions.title: Missing nonReentrant on batchMint + balanceOf-driven nudge payout (ERC777/rebasing/FoT)
decisions.reason: Sub-issues (B) rebasing, (C) fee-on-transfer, (D) double-entry-point are all C4 known-invalid (non-standard ERC-20 tokens) and DROPPED. Surviving substance is sub-issue (A): missing nonReentrant on batchMint as defense-in-depth, which has no demonstrated H/M exploit against tokens the project actually uses. Reframe as QA recommendation to add ReentrancyGuard.

decisions.title: Nudge setters apply atomically without sweep or pause; rotation strands; no kill-switch
decisions.reason: Sub-issue (C) owner-front-runs-user and (E) config-driven DOS = owner centralization (intentional per CLAUDE.md) + reckless-admin-mistake (C4 known-invalid). DROPPED. Sub-issue (A) stranded funds on token rotation has no H/M exploit on its own. Sub-issue (D) kill-switch race only matters if DEDUP-001 is unmitigated. Sub-issue (B) rotation-back jackpot is a genuine mempool race but contingent and bounded — best framed as QA hardening tied to DEDUP-001 mitigation surface.

decisions.title: ERC1155 onReceived hook reentrancy in mint loop with live max approval
decisions.reason: Legitimate reentrancy vulnerability via ERC1155 _safeMint receiver hook combined with live max approval to nftMinter and missing nonReentrant on batchMint. Distinct from DEDUP-002's ERC777-on-nudge-payout angle (different surface, different state). Not addressed by any documented intentional design. PoC must verify NFTMinterV2 uses _safeMint (not _mint) before promotion. Severity hint: high (medium-high pending PoC verification).

decisions.title: No guard preventing nudgePaymentToken == NFTStaker.rewardToken (phUSD)
decisions.reason: In the documented production wiring (single dispatcher, paymentToken == rewardToken == phUSD), the existing distinctness guard incidentally protects against this — no impact in deployed configuration. The 'BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook recipient misconfigured' scenario is reckless-admin-mistake (C4 known-invalid). The multi-dispatcher with non-phUSD scenario is speculation about future code (discouraged per project guidelines). Reframe as QA hardening: add immutable rewardToken collision guard.

decisions.title: Nudge subsidizes uneconomic minting → latestPrice ladder inflation → NFTStaker runway collapse
decisions.reason: Cross-contract economic finding. The CLAUDE.md M-03 fix (sizing R against staked subset) does not cover this attack vector — attacker manipulates latestPrice from the BatchNFTMinter side via uneconomic mints. Not documented as intentional in CLAUDE.md. APY-as-floor / S = totalStaked * latestPrice semantics are documented as intentional but they amplify rather than mitigate this attack. Severity hint: medium.

decisions.title: Unbounded count → single-tx latestPrice flash spike → transient NFTStaker runway collapse
decisions.reason: Not a clean theft path (mint-debt feedback into V partly self-funds the attack), but a tail-risk griefing concern. Not addressed by any documented intentional design. Cap on count is cheap mitigation analogous to NFTStaker's MAX_TARGET_APY bound. Severity hint: low/QA.
